proposed_core_edits.name: \omega_x(p_x)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem is tangential to the fixed-support multinomial face.  The previous ambient supremum could be positive only in an infeasible direction at a boundary law, so it did not imply motion in any relative neighborhood.  Restricting the displayed supremum to row-sum-zero directions that vanish on structural zero cells makes the observable diagnostic exactly match the theorem's neighborhood and proof.

proposed.name: \omega_x(p_x)
proposed.def: \(\sup \max_{s\in\mathcal I_x(p_x)}\|(I-\bar a_{x,s}\bar a_{x,s}^\top)Da_{x,s}(p_x)[h]\|\), where the supremum is over \(h\) satisfying \(\|h\|=1\), \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A,\,y\in\{0,1\}}h_{zay}=0\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and \(h_{zay}=0\) whenever \(p_{xzay}=0\); set the supremum to zero when no such unit direction exists, and set \(\bar a_{x,s}=a_{x,s}/\|a_{x,s}\|\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The structural assumptions are conditions on a latent extension, not literally on the observable marginal alone.  This replacement types the class as observable laws admitting such an extension and leaves response-fiber compatibility as the proved consequence of that extension rather than as a redundant additional restriction.

A numerical solver's internal gap is not a mathematical certificate.  This replacement exposes the maximization variables and interval constraints, orients primal feasibility as a lower bound and dual feasibility as an upper bound, gives the dual inequalities explicitly, and permits a reported gap only after those inequalities are verified.

prose_updates.tldr: Randomized minimax regret under partial identification is not new: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye already analyze randomized statistical rules in a finite-sample Gaussian-likelihood decision problem.  For the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, this paper instead identifies the full categorical-instrument joint action-mean polytope and its complete population minimax correspondence.  The exact three-action witness has joint rule \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\) and value \(3/16\), whereas rectangularization selects \((0,0,1)\) with value \(1/4\); an exact rational matrix certifies all ten projected vertices, and uniform-response-type perturbations retain a value gap of at least \(1/32\) with full observed support.  On separated nondegenerate unique faces, the response bases and active saddle face are stable, but the observable table moves the active left-hand coefficient matrix; this yields the derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\) and a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian policy-and-value law.  At the displayed codimension-one face intersection, class-uniform honest contraction fails at every vanishing rate absent separation, while the Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber union retains exact correspondence containment and the deployed certificate uses verified primal and dual feasibility rather than a solver-reported gap.

project_justification.gap: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye already supply a direct finite-sample Gaussian decision theory for randomized minimax-regret rules under partial identification, including multiplicity and least-randomizing refinements.  Song et al.'s model M1 supplies the latent categorical-instrument response structure.  Neither antecedent gives the sharp population minimax correspondence obtained by projecting its response fiber, the derivative of the plug-in optimizer when the observable multinomial table moves the regret matrix itself, or exact confidence-fiber containment of that correspondence.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies the binary-outcome, finite-covariate-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1 and links its sharp joint response-type polytope to a finite randomized saddle program.  Its contribution is the categorical-IV population correspondence, moving-basis and moving-coefficient inference on separated nondegenerate unique faces, and exact set-valued containment across face intersections.  It does not claim to originate randomized minimax regret under partial identification and does not subsume Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye's finite-sample admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing theory.
project_justification.fill: The response-fiber construction and feasible-basis program enumerate every population-optimal randomized mixture and expose observable pure-rule certificates.  On separated faces, explicit basis, slack, rank, reduced-cost, and active-weight margins keep the response roster and saddle face fixed; differentiating the active equations yields \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\), followed by a uniform finite-alphabet Gaussian approximation.  The negative result isolates one internal codimension-one submodel where uniform honest contraction at any vanishing rate is impossible without separation, and the Bonferroni confidence-fiber union supplies the noncontracting validity fallback.  Numerical deployment is auditable because a feasible primal response law gives a lower bound, a feasible dual tuple gives an upper bound, and only their verified bracket is called a numerical gap.

prose_updates.related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered here when every spike is feasible.  The closest direct decision-theoretic antecedent is MontielOleaQiuStoye2026DecisionTheory: it studies randomized minimax-regret statistical rules under partial identification in a finite-sample Gaussian likelihood, proves multiplicity results, and develops admissibility, least-randomizing, and profiled-regret refinements.  This paper neither claims the first randomized minimax-regret analysis under partial identification nor subsumes those results.  Its different mathematical object is the sharp categorical-IV population correspondence; its regular inference result differentiates an active saddle system whose left-hand matrix moves with the observable response-basis projections, while its finite-sample fallback contains the entire optimizer correspondence.  Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules and MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics concern different repeated-sample or local-Gaussian treatment-choice problems.  Cui2021PartialIDDecisions randomizes a binary action from marginal contrast bounds rather than optimizing three or more actions against a joint categorical-instrument response polytope.  SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies model M1's response structure; response-fiber compatibility here is derived from exogeneity, consistency, and exclusion rather than imposed again.  SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret provide background response-function and finite-saddle ingredients.  HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL studies a broader overlapping bound-agnostic class and releases a multicategory implementation; the exact and full-support perturbed witnesses are concrete regression targets for its coordinatewise-rectangle decision rule, while the present response-basis and KKT theorem does not transfer by class inclusion.  BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the separated-face analysis; KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence concern adjacent fixed-coefficient formulations, whereas here the derivative contains the moving-left-hand term \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\).  FangSantos2019DirectionalInference motivates derivative-aware inference for nonsmooth maps.  No named method is claimed to be refuted by the internal face-intersection result.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact witness shows why joint partial-identification geometry matters for categorical treatment choice: the feasible inequality \(\mu_0\leq\mu_2\) changes both the optimal randomized policy and its sharp worst-case regret relative to coordinatewise rectangularization.  The uniform-response-type perturbation shows that the discrepancy persists with positive observed cells, positive treatment support, and nondegenerate conditional outcomes, although only a conservative \(1/32\) value gap and disjoint optimizer neighborhoods are asserted away from the exact law.  The decision criterion itself has a direct antecedent in Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye.  The theorem-level payoff here is instead that, on separated unique faces, observable-table perturbations preserve the response-basis roster and active saddle face while changing the active facet coefficients; implicit differentiation therefore gives \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\) and an ordinary root-\(n\) Gaussian law.  At face intersections the paper falls back to exact confidence-fiber containment, and deployed regret is bounded by a verified dual-feasible upper certificate rather than by an unverified numerical gap.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian policy-and-regret law is restricted to the observable nondegenerate unique-face class with fixed-support, response-basis, rank, slack, reduced-cost, and active-weight margins.  Its facet-motion diagnostic is tangential to the relevant fixed-support multinomial face.  The theorem is a plug-in limit result for a categorical-instrument moving polytope, not a replacement for Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye's finite-sample Gaussian admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing analysis.  The face-intersection theorem is existential and internal to the maintained model: one displayed codimension-one local submodel rules out the specified class-uniform honest contraction at every vanishing rate absent separation.  The Bonferroni confidence-fiber union remains valid but may be conservative and noncontracting.  A numerical regret gap is valid only when explicit primal and dual feasibility inequalities are verified; otherwise the binary-outcome bound one is the vacuous fallback.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The maintained causal model is the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, with finite randomized instrument support, categorical treatment, response-type exogeneity, consistency, exclusion, and positive stratum--instrument support.  Response-fiber compatibility is a consequence of those latent structural conditions, not an additional defining restriction.  Response-function projection and finite randomized-regret programming are background ingredients.  Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye already analyze randomized minimax-regret statistical decisions under partial identification in a finite-sample Gaussian likelihood; this paper claims neither priority for that criterion nor coverage of their admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing theory.  The delivered objects are the sharp categorical-IV population optimizer correspondence, its moving-basis and moving-coefficient limit law on separated nondegenerate unique faces, exact confidence-fiber correspondence containment, and a deployed regret upper bound backed by explicit dual feasibility.  Without separation, only the internal existential face-intersection obstruction and noncontracting set-valued validity are claimed.

statement_notes.justification: Mathematical payoff.  Unlike fixed-coefficient, random-right-hand-side linear-program limits, the observable multinomial table changes the active regret coefficients themselves.  The stable-face KKT equations therefore yield the explicit derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\) and a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian law for both the unique policy and its regret value.
statement_notes.gap: Closest-prior boundary.  Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye study randomized minimax-regret statistical treatment rules under partial identification in a finite-sample Gaussian likelihood, including multiplicity, admissibility, profiled regret, and least-randomizing refinements.  This theorem instead gives the fixed-law plug-in law for the categorical-IV population policy and value when the sharp response polytope and its active left-hand coefficients move with the observable table; it does not subsume their decision theory.
statement_notes.consumer: Regular and irregular regimes.  On separated nondegenerate unique faces the theorem supplies an influence representation and Gaussian approximation.  At face intersections the paper makes no Gaussian contraction claim and retains exact finite-sample correspondence containment as the uniform validity statement.
